samples.summary: Per-cell uncached `Intl.NumberFormat` construction in the new selection-wide scans lets a collaborator-controlled cell count freeze a peer's main thread on a single toolbar click
samples.evidence: `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4318, 4335) now runs `selectionRendersAt` / `unsetKeepsRendering` over every populated cell of the selection before writing. For each cell, `selectionRendersAt` calls `renderedDecimals` → `currencyDecimals` (format.ts:149-161), which constructs a fresh `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {style:'currency', currency})` with no cache — and `unsetKeepsRendering` calls `formatValue` twice per cell (sheet.ts:4434-4435), each of which builds a formatter via `toLocaleString`. `unsetRangeStyleValues` then adds an `await this.store.get(anchor)` per cell (sheet.ts:4554). Intl formatter construction is on the order of 10s-100s of microseconds, and construction that *throws* (a hostile or malformed `cu` written by a peer, caught at format.ts:156) is slower still. Attack: a collaborator on a shared Yorkie document populates ~100k cells carrying `nf:'currency'` with a junk `cu`; the victim presses Decrease Decimals with select-all active and the UI thread blocks for many seconds, repeating on every press. Before this change the select-all path did no per-cell work at all (setRangeStyle's 'all' branch only merges `sheetStyle`), so this is newly introduced amplification. I could not measure the wall-clock cost in this environment, hence low confidence; the impact is client-side availability only, so severity is minor. Mitigation: memoise `currencyDecimals` per (locale, currency) and short-circuit the scans once a disagreement is found.

samples.summary: `clampDecimals` does not validate its `fallback`, so `getActiveDecimalState` can return an unbounded `dp` derived from an attacker-written value string, contradicting the clamp's documented guarantee
samples.evidence: `clampDecimals(dp, fallback)` returns `fallback` verbatim when `dp` is `undefined` or non-finite (format.ts:26-28); only the `dp` argument is bounded to [0, 20]. At sheet.ts:4295 the fallback is `rendersRaw ? valueDp : 2`, where `valueDp = decimalsInValue(cell?.v)` (sheet.ts:4286) is `value.length - dotIndex - 1` with no bound (format.ts:133-139). A peer writing a cell value of `'0.' + '0'.repeat(1_000_000)` directly into the shared Yorkie document — or an import producing one — makes `getActiveDecimalState()` return `dp: 1000000`, and the same value is returned unclamped from the `rendersRaw && !explicitDp` branch at sheet.ts:4303. Today this does not reach Intl: `changeDecimals` re-clamps with `Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)` at sheet.ts:4317, so the RangeError/DoS chain is broken one level up. The defect is that the guarantee is asserted in the doc comment ("never a count outside the range a cell can render at", sheet.ts:4251-4252 and 4270-4274) but is actually enforced by the caller, not the clamp — any future caller of `getActiveDecimalState` that trusts the comment and forwards `dp` to `Intl` re-opens the exact RangeError-on-paint vector this diff exists to close. Fix: clamp the fallback too, or clamp `valueDp` at its source. Confidence medium because I traced the unbounded value into the return but confirmed no current caller forwards it to Intl.
